$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. architect.rationale: Diamond. graph_agents IS a git repo (orchestrator verified rev-parse, log entry 1), so worktree isolation and rollback exist. Three slices, three disjoint file sets, zero intersection: s1 = {postmortem.py, test_postmortem.py}; s2 = {check-return-cap.py (new), test_check_return_cap.py (new)}; s3 = {audit-fleet.py, test_audit_fleet.py}, all under graph_agents/.graph/. Each done_when is a standalone test invocation that passes or fails without the other two having run. No slice touches .claude/agents/** or .claude/skills/**, so step 0.5 rule 2 does not force single-loop. The one file all three would otherwise have wanted -- CURRENT-STATE.md -- is deliberately in NO slice and left to the close; that single decision is what keeps the sets disjoint. The only near-edge is that s2 needs the lane-identity rule (a lane is real once it has a start or tool event) that currently lives in postmortem.py:read_lanes; s2 COPIES those ~10 lines from HEAD rather than importing postmortem.py, which would make s2 depend on s1's branch and collapse the diamond. Copy-don't-couple, the house pattern, applied inside one repo. Three builders in three worktrees concurrently is also the only honest way to load-test the 2026-09-19 append lock under real contention, which is the run's second purpose -- but the shape is earned by the disjointness, not by that.

plan.intent: Gap #19's open core: a machine check for GRAPH.md section 3 rule 3's three-line return cap, prose since 2026-09-03 with nothing enforcing it. New read-only reporter `python graph_agents/.graph/check-return-cap.py <run-id>` plus its test. RULING 1 (scout unknown A): it reads TRANSCRIPTS. state.json holds no return text at all, and activity.jsonl's `say` is collapsed to one line and capped at 220 chars (record-activity.py:139,171-180), so it is structurally incapable of counting lines -- a state.json-only checker cannot check the thing the rule caps. So: derive ~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/<session_id>/subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl, walk it, take the LAST message.content block of type text as the node's return -- last_said_by's definition, uncapped. YES, I am taking the coupling to an undocumented Claude Code storage layout, deliberately and for the second time; record-activity.py took it 2026-09-11 for tokens/say and the layout has held since. Conditions: (a) COPY the path derivation and the text-block walk into the new file, do NOT import record-activity.py -- a hook is executed by Claude Code and a checker importing it inherits its failure modes; (b) a missing, unreadable, empty or text-block-free transcript is NEVER a failure -- it is counted and reported as 'unverifiable: N node(s)' and the script still exits 0, the same silent-on-failure rule last_said_by follows. Exit 1 is reserved for a return found on disk and over cap. RULING 2 (scout unknown B): a 4+-line transcript return with a compliant 3-line state.json key is a DEFECT and is reported as one. The cap protects the orchestrator's context window, and the orchestrator reads the RETURN, not the key; a tidy key does not un-spend context already spent. state.json is neither the source of truth nor the excuse, and is not consulted for return content at all. RULING 3: exemptions are DATA, not prose -- a module-level EXEMPT set of architect and ops, with GRAPH.md section 3 rule 3 cited in a comment as the authority (both are gate material and say so in their own files). RULING 4: a line is a non-empty line of the final text block after strip(); blank and whitespace-only lines are not counted, so a 3-line block with a trailing newline is 3. Cap = 3. agent_id -> agent_type comes from the run's own activity.jsonl start/tool events, the only place that mapping exists; copy the lane-identity rule from HEAD's postmortem.py rather than importing it. HARD CONSTRAINT: the script NEVER echoes transcript text, not one character, not truncated, not as context for a violation -- it prints agent type, agent id and line count. A checker that quotes the thing it polices turns every report into a transcript excerpt.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

findings.issue: last_return_text() takes the last message.content block of type text, but a node's RETURN is the `message` argument of its SubagentHandback tool_use; the text block after it is post-handback chatter the orchestrator never received. Concrete: live run 2026-09-20-fleet-gaps, lane scout a38815a94d3c49662 - real return (SubagentHandback input.message) is 3 non-empty lines, compliant; the script prints 'OVER CAP: scout a38815a94d3c49662 -- 4 line(s)' and exits 1. Same for builder a5ec4987f85a61ee3: real return 2 lines, script says 10. Both of the run's reported violations are false positives, which is the worst possible failure for a checker whose exit 1 is meant to be actionable. It cuts the other way too: reviewer a72a137913f042f54's real return is 3 lines while the script measured an unrelated 1-line block - right verdict, wrong evidence, so a genuinely over-cap handback can be missed. Fix: prefer the LAST SubagentHandback tool_use's input.message; fall back to the last text block only when no handback exists.

An in-flight lane is reported as a compliant checked return. Concrete: during this review, lanes a1e12e2ad1379b837 and ab73cbde6ad43d096 (reviewers still running, zero SubagentHandback events) were printed as '1 line(s)' - their last text block was an opening sentence, not a return. A lane that has not returned yet should be 'unverifiable', not silently certified within cap. Falls out of the same fix: no handback on disk => no return to check.

The fixtures encode the same wrong model: write_transcript() and every hand-built transcript contain only {'type':'text'} blocks and no SubagentHandback tool_use at all, so no case in the suite could ever have distinguished a return from trailing chatter. The suite is well built and genuinely fails when broken (I verified both injected faults), but it asserts the implementation's definition rather than the behaviour rule 3 caps. A corrected suite needs at least one fixture with a compliant handback followed by a longer text block, asserting NOT a violation.

Note, not a blocker: the scout's transcript-layout finding stopped at 'the return text survives in the transcript' and did not carry the shape it survives IN (a SubagentHandback tool_use payload), which is what the architect then mis-specified as 'the last text block, last_said_by's definition'. last_said_by is right for a heartbeat caption and wrong for a return; the copy was faithful, the source rule was not applicable.

Explicit ruling on whether the on-disk message is what the orchestrator received. It is. cross_slice_findings.contradiction_test: The decisive test -- does s1 call a lane phantom while s2 reports a return for it? -- comes back EMPTY: the intersection of s1's 96 phantom stop ids with s2's 10 node ids is the empty set. The copy-don't-couple call holds here; if a future slice changes the lane KEY (the `id or agent` fallback) in one file and not the other, that agreement breaks silently, and nothing currently checks it.
